title: Odisha government plans 870-Acre Silicon Valley hub in Cuttack’s Naraj for semiconductor, IT projects
author: Satyasundar Barik
content_html:
The Mohan Majhi Government has announced plans to develop Odisha Silicon Valley over an area of 870 acres near Naraj, in Cuttack district, which will host all major semiconductor, electronics, and IT projects.

“The area for Odisha Silicon Valley in Naraj offers a highly favourable strategic location from the standpoint of connectivity and industrial infrastructure. With seamless connectivity to the Cuttack–Bhubaneswar urban corridor, the site also provides efficient multimodal access to major ports such as Paradip and Dhamra, along with connectivity to key national highways,” said Mr. Majhi while attending SEMICON India 2026 in New Delhi on Friday (September 18, 2026).

“Naraj will be a potential strategic hub for the semiconductor supply chain, logistics and allied industries,” said Odisha CM in a statement.

“Semiconductor fabrication facilities and assembly units require reliable access to substantial quantities of water and power, and the site’s proximity to the Mahanadi River provides a significant locational advantage for meeting industrial water requirements. Combined with its connectivity and infrastructure potential, Naraj offers a strong foundation for developing a world-class semiconductor and electronics ecosystem,” he pointed out.

Stating that Odisha was looking to build on its growing investment pipeline and attract the next wave of investments across the semiconductor value chain, he informed that the State government received investment proposals worth approximately ₹23,600 crore and the potential to generate 6,100 employment opportunities, marking a significant step towards building a robust semiconductor and electronics ecosystem.

According to Chief Minister’s Office, Mr. Majhi interacted with delegations from Japan, Sweden and Taiwan.

As per supportive policy, Odisha has extended 25% additional fiscal support to India Semiconductor Mission-approved projects in semiconductor equipment manufacturing, semiconductor-grade gases, raw materials and supply-chain segments. The current policy framework also provides support for engineer relocation, manpower skilling, internships, international patents and R&D.

title: Amid strong El Niño, Wayanad sees sharp rise in September temperatures
author: Sam Paul A.
content_html:
Amid concerns over a strong El Niño, climate data released by the Hume Weather Lab of the Hume Centre for Ecology and Wildlife Biology show a notable rise in temperatures in Wayanad in the first half of September. Between September 1 and 17, 2026, the average maximum temperature in the hill district stood at 29.2°C, around 1.9°C higher than the average for the previous three years, with experts warning of potential impacts on water resources and agriculture.

The average high during this period was 27.3°C in 2023, 27.2°C in 2024, and 27.3°C in 2025.

For seven consecutive days, from September 11 to 17, the maximum temperature remained above 30°C. The highest temperature recorded during the period was 30.7°C on September 15. The highest temperature recorded in Wayanad in 2026 was 34.4°C in summer on April 18.

Along with the rise in air temperature, higher soil temperatures were also recorded. Between September 1 and 17, soil temperatures rose to as high as 39°C. Readings above 30°C were recorded on several days. A significant difference was also observed between soil temperatures measured in open and shaded locations.

The data also reveal that Wayanad received below-normal rainfall between September 1 and 17. Only four days of light, isolated rainfall were recorded during the period. While 34 mm of rain was recorded on September 14, 61 mm was recorded in the Lakkidi area on September 17.

C.K. Vishnudas, executive director of the Hume Centre for Ecology and Wildlife Biology, said the unusually high temperatures could increase water stress, accelerate groundwater depletion and affect crops in Wayanad.

“The water table could decline rapidly as groundwater levels fall. Wetland crops, particularly paddy, could be severely affected by water stress, while cultivated plants in general may also face greater pressure. I recently observed a coffee plant flowering in September, possibly in response to heat stress. Normally, flowering occurs during December, January and February. Such off-season responses need to be closely observed to understand how crops respond to these conditions. This is perhaps the first time we are observing such impacts in the district against the backdrop of a super El Niño,” he said.

The Hume Centre data indicate that Wayanad has started to experience a hot and relatively dry spell even before the southwest monsoon begins to withdraw, with higher daytime and soil temperatures coinciding with low rainfall. Though the average minimum temperature during the period was 20.9°C, the high soil temperatures point to significant surface heating in the district.

According to experts, the observations underline the need for greater attention to water management. Planning is needed across sectors to reduce water stress and manage water-related risks arising from such weather conditions, Mr. Vishudas added.

title: Bihar announces OTS scheme for brick kilns, waives ₹90 crore interest on outstanding dues
author: Amit Bhelari
content_html:
Bihar government on Friday (September 18, 2026) came out with a One-Time Settlement (OTS) scheme for the settlement of outstanding dues of brick kilns for brick kiln season 2024-25.

Under the scheme, brick kiln owners will have to deposit outstanding principal dues, while the interest component, which had accumulated on their earlier dues, will be waived off by the State government, Mr. Kumar told reporters at his official chamber at Vikas Bhawan. 

He added that brick kiln owners owe a total of ₹316.66 crore, comprising ₹226.40 crore in outstanding royalty and ₹90.26 crore in interest.

Out of ₹316.66 crore outstanding dues, only ₹27.28 crore has been recovered by the District Mining Officers concerned through certificate proceedings/FIRs, thus leaving ₹289.38 crore as outstanding amount that includes ₹203 crore as principal amount while ₹85 crore as interest component. 

“In Bihar, those engaged in the brick-kiln business had a substantial amount of money outstanding with the government for a long period. They had also been demanding that arrangements be made for them to pay the outstanding amount in a lump sum. We considered their plea and, accordingly, the state cabinet, in its last meeting, decided to bring an OTS scheme for those engaged in the business of brick kilns in the State,” Mr. Kumar said while speaking to the press in Patna.

“I would like to thank the Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary for bringing the scheme under which a one-time payment can be made, and substantial relief has been provided to those engaged in the brick-kiln business,” he said, adding that the move will increase the government’s revenue, while also providing considerable relief to people engaged in this business. 

The scheme will be applicable for a period of three months between September 21 and December 20, 2026, during which brick kiln owners will have to deposit the entire amount, failing which they will have to pay the entire dues under the earlier system, including the full interest. There are people associated with approximately 6,000 brick kilns. 

The minister appealed to all the brick-kiln owners to deposit the one-time amount within the stipulated period so that they can restart their businesses afresh and do not face any difficulties in the future. 

Changes in rules 

While talking about the department approving “Bihar District Mineral Foundation (Amendment) Rules 2026 that brought certain changes in the earlier 2018 Rules, Mr. Kumar said that 2% amount is deposited in each district from where mineral extraction takes place, where minerals such as stone or sand are excavated. A district associated with mining receives this two per cent amount.

Following the amendments to the Rules, 70% of District Mineral Foundation (DMF) will be spent in the block from where the minerals are being extracted, while 30% will be spent in other blocks of the district, Mr. Kumar said, adding that earlier, the ratio was 60:40.

Another change is that elected members such as Members of Parliament, Members of Legislative Assembly, and Members of Legislative Council from different districts were previously not members of the District Mineral Foundation (DMF), the Minister said, adding that they will now also be members of the DMF following the change in the Rules.

He asserted that the auction of stone-mining areas has also been completed in Nawada and Sheikhpura and the auction in other districts will be carried out as quickly as possible.

The Minister said that Union Minister of State for Coal and Mines Satish Chandra Dubey will be visiting the state on September 22 (2026) and “we will have a meeting with the Geological Survey of India (GSI) along with him. Our objective is to move forward in the mineral sector as quickly as possible and expedite the work.

title: Sharad Pawar urges Maharashtra government to declare drought, provide ₹50,000 per hectare relief
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
NCP (SP) leader Sharad Pawar has written to Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, urging him to provide relief of ₹50,000 per hectare and declare drought based on the actual damage, taluka-wise rainfall, and crop condition in Maharashtra. 

“Instead of taking a decision based solely on the average district figures, the actual damage should be considered together based on taluka-wise rainfall, crop condition, and declare drought,” said Mr. Pawar, adding that the situation is dire in most of the state and in some districts, there is a deficit of about 60% of the average in the last three months.

This year, when looking at the average rainfall deficit by region from June to August, Marathwada has seen a 69% deficit, Vidarbha a 61% deficit, Konkan a 33% deficit and some districts in western and northern Maharashtra a 26% deficit, he stated in the letter. 

He listed nine measures, suggesting Mr. Fadnavis to end drought without waiting for formal announcements.

The list includes that farmers should receive ₹50,000 per hectare as an aid, while agricultural labourer families should be given special assistance of ₹25,000 each; the banks should be instructed to expedite the implementation of the loan waiver scheme and increase the incentive subsidy from Rs 50,000 to ₹1 lakh; the announced crop insurance assistance of ₹17,000 per hectare in the unseasonal rains relief package last year should also be distributed immediately, and others. 

According to him, at least 31 out of 36 districts in the state have received much less rainfall than the average. The state has received only 748 mm of rainfall from June 1 to September 15, which is a 19% decrease compared to the average.

Mr. Pawar also recommended implementing a one-rupee crop insurance scheme and designing special schemes to be implemented through the Employment Guarantee Scheme. For instance: carry out water conservation and other agricultural-related works. 

For livestock, Mr. Pawar has asked to make arrangements of fodder, water, and necessary veterinary services for livestock.

“State and district-level control rooms should be set up to monitor rainfall, crop condition, water scarcity, fodder availability and livestock condition daily in each district. District Collectors should be given the power to make ‘Negative Debit’ to provide additional funds from the treasury,” the letter read. 

The other measure includes relief for students by not only waiving examination fees but also the entire educational fees of students studying in schools, colleges and other educational institutions in drought-affected talukas.
